properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 4 at 3:51PM CDT until August 6 at 1:00PM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Three Rivers affecting Live Oak County.

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Three Rivers.

* WHEN...Until Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 35.0 feet, Major lowland flooding occurs. Flow backs
up minor creeks to the slabs of lowest homes in the River Creek
Acres Subdivision, five miles southeast of George West, requiring
evacuations. Livestock are cut off and could drown in low areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:15 PM CDT Tuesday the stage was 34.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 20.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
Thursday morning and continue falling to 9.2 feet early Sunday
afternoon.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Petersville Area

* WHEN...Until 500 PM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Low-water
crossings are inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 842 AM AKDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges
indicated heavy rain across the warned area. Flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly. Between 2 and 3 inches
of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to
1.5 inches are possible.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

Southwestern Colfax County in northeastern New Mexico...
North Central Mora County in northeastern New Mexico...

* Until 500 PM MDT.

Ocate, or 25 miles west of Springer, moving southeast at 10 mph.

HAZARD...Golf ball size hail and 60 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Trained spotters reported.

IMPACT...People and animals outdoors will be injured. Expect hail
damage to roofs, siding, windows, and vehicles. Expect
wind damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Ocate and Rayado.
properties.instruction:
Anyone outdoors should move to shelter inside a well-built structure
and stay away from windows. This storm has produced dangerous hail
and is capable of producing damaging winds.

Heavy rains from severe thunderstorms can produce sudden and
dangerous flows in arroyos, ditches and over low water crossings. Do
not attempt to drive through areas where water covers the roadway.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Yentna River including Lake Creek.

* WHEN...Until 100 PM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 804 AM AKDT, The river gauge at the Yentna River at Lake
Creek indicates rises in water levels from heavy rain across
the warned area. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly. Between 1.5 and 3 inches of rain have fallen.
Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are possible
with higher amounts possible in the upper Yentna Basin.
- For Yentna River at Lake Creek:
At 7:51am the stage was 20.7 feet.
Flood Stage is 20.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest near 22 feet is expected Wednesday.

Impacts:
Between 21 and 22 feet, several lodges may have water in or
around low-lying cabins.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
